title: Keep the joint clock law when predicting rare circulation
statement: The parity-dependent conserving family has a corrected-current martingale with variance factor1-alpha^2. For gamma_N->infinity but gamma_N/N->0, its matching scalar rate isq^2/[2s m(1-m)(1-alpha^2)T] under the canonical/o(logN)-entropy initializer, versusq^2/[2s m(1-m)T] for independent controls. The earlier strict upper obstruction permits more general deterministic starts; the matching lower bound does not. Retaining a detailed initial occupancy record can violate its initializer. No full slow-common-clock spatial action follows.

The separate matching slow-common-clock SCALAR law needs its canonical or o(logN) conditional initial-entropy premise. Identical individual clock laws do not determine joint control correlations. Actual selective ports, common mean, full future conditional native-and-clock law, conservation, timing/sensing and vanishing reciprocal implementation errors are supplied, not acquired from finite observations.
